solves: Composes the label, the control, the help text and the error message of a form field, and carries the error state. It names and describes the control it wraps, or names the group of radios or checkboxes it wraps.
use_when: When a control needs a name, a required mark, an explanation or an error message.
To name a group of radios or checkboxes, such as Payment method, and carry its error message.
required when filling in the field is required.
help when the expected value needs an explanation.
error only with the sentence that says what to fix.
do_not_use_when: For a control that already brings its own visible name, such as nph-checkbox alone.
To show an error on a disabled field: whoever cannot edit cannot fix.
To leave the field red without a text that explains.
With a loose nph-label inside the field, besides its label.
With the placeholder of the control in place of the label: it disappears when the person types.
As a box to gain space between blocks.

label.constraint: The label text, already localized by the consuming application, drawn by an nph-label. It is also the accessible name of the control: the field writes it on the control, or names the group with it. Empty, the field renders anyway and emits console.error in development.

required.constraint: The Figma `obrigatório`. Shows the asterisk on the label and writes required on the control, which announces it. In a group of radios, the group carries aria-required; a group of checkboxes or switches has only the asterisk.

info.constraint: The Figma `ícone`. The text of the explanation, passed to the nph-label, which draws the information icon and opens the nph-tooltip with it. It never repeats the help text.

info-label.constraint: The accessible name of the information icon, such as More information about Email, passed to the nph-label. The property is infoLabel. Without it the icon does not show.

help.constraint: The Figma `mostrar apoio` and `texto de apoio`. The help line, in text/caption. Empty, it is not drawn. It leaves the line while the error shows.

error.constraint: The Figma `mensagem de erro`. Filling it in is what makes the field invalid: there is no state property. The message replaces the help, in text/body-md and status/error, with no icon, and the field writes invalid on the control. A disabled field hides it.

counter.constraint: The Figma `contador` and `texto do contador`. The counter text, shown as it comes, such as 12/500: at the end of the help line, or on a line of its own below the error. The field counts nothing, and the counter is not part of the description of the control.

disabled.constraint: Written on the control, which fades itself with state/disabled-opacity; the field draws no opacity, and the label and the message line never fade. Disabled wins over error. A disabled fieldset around the field hides the error too, except in its first legend, as the browser does. When the field is enabled again, it gives back only the disabled it turned on.

slot.constraint: The Figma `⮑ controle`. One control, such as nph-input, or the options of a group of checkboxes, radios or switches. An option declares itself with the static nphFieldRole of its class, option or radio; anything else is a control.

error.choose_when: The Figma `state` `erro`: when the value needs correction, always with the message filled in. In code, it is the presence of error.

required.choose_when: The Figma `obrigatório`: when filling in the field is required.

info.choose_when: The Figma `ícone`: when the field needs a short explanation that does not fit in the label or in the help; in code, info with info-label.

default.token: space/stack-tight between the label row, the control and the message line
default.changes_for_user: The label, the control and, when filled in, the help line. With no help, no error and no counter, the message line is not drawn and keeps no height.

error.token: text/body-md and status/error on the message
error.changes_for_user: The error message replaces the help and the control shows its error state. The label does not change.

disabled.changes_for_user: The control fades and does not respond. The error is hidden and the help comes back; the label and the message line do not fade.

business_rules: Filling in the error message is what makes the field invalid; there is no error state without the sentence.
The help text leaves the line while the error shows: write the rule in the error message too.
Disabled wins over error: a disabled field shows no error, because whoever cannot edit cannot fix.
Inside a field, the field is the source of label, description, invalid and required of its control; a value set on the control is overwritten.
domain_errors: error: the value needs correction; the message says what to fix.
ai_hints: Give the control its name with the label of nph-field; do not add a loose nph-label or an aria-label on the control.
Write error to put the field in error: there is no state property and no invalid on the field.
Set required, disabled and error on the field, not on the control: the field writes them on the control.
In a group of radios or checkboxes, put the options in the slot of one nph-field: it names the group and carries the message.
Do not wrap nph-checkbox alone in nph-field to give it a name: its text already is.
The counter text comes ready from the application; the field does not count characters.

accessibility.semantics: The label is an nph-label without for. A control is named and described by properties the field writes on it, because an id does not cross a shadow root. In a group, the slot is wrapped in a group, or a radiogroup for radios, inside the shadow root of the field.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label of nph-field is the only name of the control: the field writes it as label, and the control puts it on its focusable element. A group is named by the label through aria-label.
keyboard: Tab reaches the information icon of the label, when it exists, and then the control.
The keyboard of the control is the control's own.
accessibility.focus: The field takes no focus. The focus shows on the wrapped control; a click on the label text moves the focus to the control. In a group, a click on the label moves no focus.
accessibility.contrast: The label uses color/foreground, 21:1 in light and 14.73:1 in dark; the control border is color/input, which meets 3:1.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error state always brings the written message; the field is never only red.

invalid_combinations: No label — the control has no name; the field renders and emits console.error in development.
error on a disabled field — disabled wins and the error is hidden.

No control in the slot, more than one control, a control mixed with options, radios mixed with checkboxes or switches, or an element that does not take the field contract — the field renders and warns in development.
anti_patterns: Leaving the field red without a text that explains.
Showing an error on a disabled field.
Putting a loose nph-label inside the field, besides its label.
Using the placeholder of the control in place of the label.
Wrapping a control that already has its own visible name, such as nph-checkbox alone.
Using the field as a box to gain space between blocks.
Setting invalid, required or the accessible name on the control inside a field.
